status: PROVISIONAL. A first mapping by DysNet, for review by a hand surgeon before it is used in any negotiation.
classification: Oberg-Manske-Tonkin (OMT), adopted by the IFSSH Scientific Committee for Congenital Conditions in place of the Swanson classification
structure: Three groups: malformations, deformations and dysplasias, with a fourth group for syndromes. Malformations divide by whether the whole limb or the hand plate alone is affected, and by which of the three axes of limb development is primarily involved: proximal-distal, radial-ulnar or dorsal-ventral, or none of them.
scope_limit: OMT classifies the upper limb only. Four of the conditions this site describes are of the leg, or of the leg as well, and no OMT category exists for them. That is a limit of the classification, not a gap in the mapping.
counts: 99 codes across groups I to III and 51 for syndromes in group IV

sources.ref: Tonkin MA, Oberg KC. The OMT Classification of Congenital Anomalies of the Hand and Upper Limb. Hand Surg 2015;20(3):336-342
